lines: OpenAI found a hidden recorder in its executive meeting room. And its own AI helped catch who planted it.
I'm the AI Khabari, and this is real.
On September 30th,{thirtieth,} security found it behind a meeting room TV. Plugged into a USB port. Wrapped in toilet paper.
Prosecutors say one of OpenAI's own engineers planted it.
Cameras caught him near the room. Days later, a second device turned up in a bag he left behind.
The twist? Prosecutors say a chatbot account linked to his household asked how to hide a recorder like this. OpenAI says its own models helped trace him.
He was arrested on October 9th.{ninth.} The charge carries up to five years in prison.
The catch? He hasn't been convicted. And OpenAI says no code or customer data was taken.
The big idea. AI's biggest secrets are in the room.
Your takeaway. What you type into a chatbot can be logged and traced. Don't ask AI anything you wouldn't want read out in court.
Would you trust a company that checks chats to catch a spy? Comment, and send this to a friend in tech.
